newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firms, U.S. arrivals pressure premiums.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firms, U.S. arrivals pressure premiums.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices firmed slightly with IPE futures on Thursday but premiums for Russian cargoes and heating oil barges were under pressure from U.S. imports, traders said. Nov IPE gas oil closed 25 cents higher at $227.75 a tonne. Traders said the rally in gas oil, which followed a dip to a low of $222 earlier, was in response to a recovery in crude.
"The overall tone of the market is overshadowed by the transatlantic arrivals," a trader said.
Large amounts of U.S. origin heating oil were being sold aggressively into the Rotterdam barge market.
Barges from storage fetched around Nov IPE +$2 fob ARA, bringing the value of refinery grade barges down to +$3.50. German diesel barges were unchanged at around Nov IPE +$34/35.
"The market is well supplied for the next two weeks," said a trader, noting buying interest was low for heating oil.
Russian for November delivery was sold at Nov IPE +$1.75 cif NWE, about 25 cents adrift from Wednesday's levels.

Prompt low sulphur diesel cargoes remained scarce, with the differential over heating oil still large at $24. But one trader said refineries had more avails for early Nov. "We have seen the tops for now. Even diesel could drift off slightly," he said.
